title: Issue #176: catalog: define X31 ecosystem data governance, information quality and lifecycle contracts
content:
State: open

## Architekturidentität

- **Architecture ID:** `ATC-CROSSCUTTING-X31-ECOSYSTEM-DATA-GOVERNANCE-INFORMATION-QUALITY-DATA-LIFECYCLE`
- **Layer:** X31 – Ecosystem Data Governance, Information Quality & Data Lifecycle
- **Status:** `PROPOSED / NOT VERIFIED`
- **Scope:** A-TownChain, GlobusOS, Aurora AI
- **Planned scope:** 17 sublayers × 10 planned function contracts = 170. This is a target, not evidence that contracts are already cataloged.

## Goal

Define a cross-ecosystem governance and integration layer for data ownership, quality, provenance, semantic consistency, retention, and controlled lifecycle management. X31 is not a second database, storage system, or alternative implementation of existing components.

## Boundaries

- **X4 – Data, State & Storage:** storage and state models remain canonical there; X31 governs cross-system data quality and accountability.
- **X11 – Privacy & Data Protection:** X31 integrates applicable privacy and information-protection controls into lifecycle governance without replacing X11.
- **X17 – Documentation & Knowledge Management:** X31 governs structured data quality/provenance/lifecycle, not technical documentation.
- **X18 – Ecosystem Integrity & Catalog Drift:** X31 supplies quality and provenance rules for data used by integrity/drift monitoring.
- **X27 – Ecosystem Knowledge & Semantic Integration:** X31 defines binding quality, ownership, and lifecycle controls.
- **X28 – Simulation & System Modeling:** model and measurement data must retain provenance, version, and quality status.

## Sublayers — 10 planned contracts each

| Sublayer | Scope / planned contract concepts |
|---|---|
| X31.01 Data Governance Registry | Data-object ID, domain, owner, steward, scope, classification, quality profile, policy binding, version status, audit reference |
| X31.02 Data Inventory & Discovery | Source registration, dataset inventory, schema discovery, storage reference, freshness, dependencies, duplicate detection, inventory timestamp, completeness, report |
| X31.03 Data Classification & Sensitivity | Classification level, confidentiality, integrity and availability needs, purpose limitation, access class, retention class, export restriction, label validation, reclassification workflow |
| X31.04 Data Quality & Metrics | Completeness, correctness, consistency, freshness, uniqueness, validity, tolerances, quality score, deviation register, remediation status |
| X31.05 Data Lineage & Provenance | Source ID, capture time, transformation step, lineage chain, producer, source hash, processing revision, provenance validation, lineage gap, audit export |
| X31.06 Schema & Version Governance | Schema ID/version, compatibility rule, migration description, field deprecation, validation rule, version binding, change approval, backward compatibility, schema audit |
| X31.07 Semantics & Canonical Data Models | Concept ID, canonical field name, unit, type, range, ontology reference, aliases, semantic validation, mapping rule, conflict report |
| X31.08 Data Integration & Transformation | Input/target schema, transformation rule, mapping version, pre/post-import validation, error handling, idempotency, integrity reconciliation, import log |
| X31.09 Replication & Consistency | Replica ID, replication mode, source/target revision, sync status, conflict detection/resolution, consistency model, retry rule, replication audit |
| X31.10 Retention & Deletion Lifecycle | Retention class, start trigger, expiry condition, deletion approval, deletion log, legal hold reason, archive rule, restore boundary, deletion verification, completion status |
| X31.11 Data Access & Usage Terms | Access policy, purpose, authorization reference, usage scope, release condition, export rule, onward-sharing check, usage log, revocation, policy evidence |
| X31.12 Data Catalog & Discoverability | Catalog ID, description, search metadata, owner contact, schema reference, quality indicator, update time, dependency link, visibility rule, catalog validation |
| X31.13 Reference & Master Data | Record ID, canonical key, validity period, duplicate rule, change source, sync rule, conflict priority, reference validation, history, approval |
| X31.14 Events, Telemetry & Time Series | Event schema, time basis, event ID, sequence validation, timestamp validation, loss indicator, deduplication, retention profile, aggregation rule, replay provenance |
| X31.15 Data Errors, Anomalies & Correction | Error ID, anomaly type, severity, affected record, cause, quarantine rule, proposed correction, correction approval, recheck, closure evidence |
| X31.16 Data Access for AI & Analytics | Dataset version, permitted purpose, training/inference role, representativeness check, quality threshold, privacy reference, provenance, access control, result traceability, usage approval |
| X31.17 Lifecycle Audit & Compliance Evidence | Lifecycle event, policy version, accountable actor, change time, audit rule, evidence reference, integrity proof, deviation classification, remediation status, audit closure |

## Required data-contract metadata

Each catalog record must identify the governed data, accountable owner, applicable quality/lifecycle rules, canonical source, and reproducible evidence. Proposed contract shape:

```yaml
architecture_id: ATC-CROSSCUTTING-X31-ECOSYSTEM-DATA-GOVERNANCE-INFORMATION-QUALITY-DATA-LIFECYCLE
layer: X31
status: PROPOSED
verification_status: NOT_VERIFIED
data_contract:
  id: ATC-X31-DATA-<DOMAIN>-<NUMBER>
  name: "<stable-data-contract-name>"
  domain: "<data-domain>"
  schema_version: "<version>"
  canonical_source: "<canonical-repository-or-registry>"
  owner: "<accountable-owner>"
  steward: "<data-steward>"
  classification: UNCLASSIFIED
  purpose: "<approved-purpose>"
quality:
  completeness_rule: "<rule-id>"
  consistency_rule: "<rule-id>"
  freshness_limit: null
  validation_rules: []
  accepted_deviations: []
  quality_status: UNASSESSED
lifecycle:
  creation_rule: "<rule-id>"
  retention_policy: "<policy-id>"
  archival_policy: "<policy-id>"
  deletion_policy: "<policy-id>"
  legal_hold: false
provenance:
  source_id: "<source-id>"
  source_revision: "<revision>"
  transformation_ids: []
  content_hash: "<hash>"
  integrity_status: UNRESOLVED
evidence:
  repository: "<canonical-repository>"
  commit_sha: "<full-40-character-sha>"
  path: "<canonical-path>"
  symbol: "<function-or-type>"
  workflow_run_id: null
  logs_hash: null
  artifacts: []
classification_status: UNRESOLVED
```

## Governance invariants

1. Every production dataset and canonical schema has an accountable owner.
2. Units, keys, types, and meanings are explicit; they must not be inferred from field names alone.
3. Transformations trace to defined sources and revisions.
4. Critical quality violations block downstream use when policy requires it, or are explicitly recorded as approved exceptions.
5. Changes to canonical schemas are versioned and compatibility-checked.
6. Retention, access, archiving, and deletion align with X11 and applicable legal requirements.
7. Critical data corrections are authorized, traceable, and auditable; no silent corrections.
8. A hash can support integrity checks for specific content but does not, by itself, prove factual correctness or provenance.

## SSOT and ownership boundaries

- `a-townchain-ecosystem`: cross-repository architecture/catalog mappings, integration, compliance, evidence, and drift control only; no duplicate data/storage/runtime implementation.
- `atc-standards`: normative technical data/protocol rules only when registered and authorized there.
- `a-townchain`: blockchain state and transaction data.
- `a-townchain/components/vm`: canonical ATC-VM and associated state access.
- `a-townchain/components/algorithm`: canonical algorithm/consensus.
- `globus-os/modules/atc-shivacore/kernel/`: canonical ShivaCore kernel.
- `globus-os`: OS services and desktop system.
- **ATCLang and Aurora AI:** verify canonical repository/path before mapping; do not guess.
- `demo-repository` remains excluded from the live drift gate.
- Catalogs should reference canonical sources rather than uncontrolled copies.
- Sensitive/personal data must retain the applicable access and protection restrictions.

## Implementation sequence

1. Inventory existing data, schema, storage, telemetry, and provenance contracts; mark duplicates and unresolved ownership.
2. Map each data type/schema to its canonical repository, path, symbol, or registry reference.
3. Define measurable quality criteria, tolerances, failure states, and accountable owners for critical data.
4. Align creation, usage, versioning, archival, and deletion with applicable policies.
5. Validate schemas and semantics at integration boundaries across blockchain, VM, GlobusOS, and Aurora AI.
6. Capture exact full commit SHAs, paths, workflow Run → Job → Step, exit codes, logs, and artifact hashes.
7. Assign statuses only from evidence: `MAPPED`, `IMPLEMENTED`, `VERIFIED`, `RESIDUAL`, `BLOCKED`, `UNRESOLVED`, or `EXCLUDED`. Green CI alone is not proof of data quality.

## Acceptance checklist (0/10)

- [ ] 17 sublayers with stable architecture IDs are recorded in the catalog.
- [ ] 170 planned function contracts are individually defined and deduplicated.
- [ ] Accountable owners and canonical data sources are mapped.
- [ ] Schema versions and semantic units are unambiguous.
- [ ] Quality metrics and measurable acceptance thresholds are defined.
- [ ] Provenance and transformations are traceably linked.
- [ ] Retention, archival, and deletion rules are aligned.
- [ ] Privacy and access controls are reconciled with X11.
- [ ] Integration and replication conflicts are testable and handled.
- [ ] Verification evidence contains exact references and artifact hashes.

## Initial status

`PROPOSED / NOT VERIFIED`

Issue creation or catalog planning is not implementation, catalog integration, or technical verification. Each contract remains unverified until mapped to canonical sources and supported by reproducible evidence.
